timed_text.text: 18. One of the biggest reasons athletes break in big moments is that they've never planned
for them. Not the success, the worst case. What happens if you fall behind early? What happens
if you make a visible error in front of the biggest crowd you've ever competed in front of?
What happens if your body starts to give out before the competition is over? Most athletes avoid
those questions. They think planning for failure invites it. That's backwards.
Planning for adversity is what makes you dangerous because now you have a response ready
before the moment hits. This is the then plan. If x happens, then I do y. It's not pessimism,
it's preparation. Research is clear on this. Athletes who pre-planned responses to adversity
recover faster and perform more consistently than athletes who respond in the moment without a
plan. You're not hoping the bad thing doesn't happen. You're deciding in advance that it
doesn't own you. On your screen, you're going to build your if-then plan for the three most likely

timed_text.text: You just made three decisions in advance.
When those moments arrive and they will,
your brain already has the answer.
No freeze, no spiral, just the plan.
Now let you finish, day 18 is complete.
